policy.t: GST 2.0: two-wheelers up to 350cc cut from 28% (+ cess) to 18%; above 350cc raised to 40%; EVs stay at 5%. TVS passed on the full benefit.
Auto PLI tenure extended by one year to 31-Mar-2028 (incentives for five consecutive years from FY24 for approved applicants).

PM E-DRIVE e-2W subsidy extended to 31-Mar-2028 at ₹2,500/kWh, capped at ₹5,000 per vehicle (or 15% of ex-factory price; price ceiling ₹1.5 lakh); e-2W allocation raised to ₹2,767 cr. The previous window had lapsed on 31-Jul-2026. The L5 e-3W subsidy closed in Dec-2025 after hitting its target.
West Asia conflict: steel, aluminium and oil-derived input costs up 3-5% of revenue; gas, labour and container shortages cut April 2026 dispatches (TVS April volumes +7% only).

moat: Distribution and service reach
Moderate
Pan-India dealer network built over decades; strongest in the south and in scooters; dealer stock kept under 30 days (cash-and-carry dealers).
Real but shared: Hero and Honda have larger rural networks.
Product breadth and launch cadence
Strong
Jupiter 110/125, Ntorq 125/150, Apache RTR/RR/RTX, Raider, Ronin, iQube, Orbiter, King 3W; JD Power top ranks (Jupiter 110, Raider, Ronin).
The main reason TVS has gained share in every year since FY21.
Brand and pricing power
Moderate
Customers pay a premium over a discounting rival in scooters (Q1FY27 call); premium motorcycles ~47% of FY26 motorcycle sales (Emkay).
Earned, not structural: rivals can and do launch into the same segments.
Cost position
Weak
EBITDA margin 12.9% vs Bajaj 20.8%, Eicher 24.7%, Hero 14.9% (FY26); material cost 71% of sales.
No cost advantage: TVS earns less per vehicle than Hero, Bajaj or Eicher.
EV capability
Strong
#1 in e-2W registrations in FY26 (24.3%) and Aug-2026 (27.1%); 1mn+ iQube built; in-house software/connected platform.
Leadership in a market where Bajaj, Ather and Hero Vida are close behind; EV profits still thin.
Export franchise
Strong
HLX built for Africa/LatAm (5mn cumulative); PT TVS in Indonesia; 2W international +31% in FY26 vs industry +12%; exports ~26% of turnover.
A genuine edge in commuter bikes for emerging markets; Bajaj is the bigger exporter.
Captive finance
Moderate
TVS Credit (book ₹32,053 cr) finances a large share of TVS retail; helps in rural and new-to-credit buyers.
Helps volumes; ties up capital and adds credit risk to the group.
critiques: Valuation: at ~36x our FY28E standalone EPS the stock trades far above its own 27x forward median since 2021 and above every 2W peer; the street’s 33-35x plus TVS Credit assumes the premium is permanent.
GAM; Nirmal Bang (HOLD: "most positives priced in"); BOBCAPS (HOLD)

Capital allocation: ~₹2,400 cr went into subsidiaries in FY26 and ~₹1,700-1,900 cr is guided for FY27; Norton lost ₹723 cr and TVS EBike ₹417 cr in FY26; the subsidiaries ex-TVS Credit lose ~₹1,300 cr a year.
Nirmal Bang; Kotak (subsidiary EBIT loss ₹380 cr in Q1FY27); BOBCAPS
Margins: 12.8-13.1% is below Hero (14.9%) and far below Bajaj (20.8%); the PLI (~0.6-0.9% of revenue) ends after FY28.
Cycle: FY27 growth benefits from the Sep-2025 GST cut; from Q3FY27 the base is high and El Niño is a risk to rural demand.
EV competition: Bajaj (22.7%), Ather (15.9%) and Hero Vida (10.5%) are close; subsidies are small (₹5,000 cap) and policy-dependent.
Governance: CMD pay 436x the median employee (+46% in FY26); KMP short-term pay ₹106 cr; group cash flowing to unlisted overseas subsidiaries.
